name: Deliver a daily digest with Airtable and Telegram end to end

nodes.name: Daily Schedule
nodes.notes: Starts the workflow on a timer — daily at 17:00. No input data; downstream nodes fetch what they need.

nodes.name: Read Source Feed
nodes.notes: Pulls the RSS feed and emits one item per entry (title, link, content). Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up.

nodes.name: Skip Already-Seen Posts
nodes.notes: Cross-execution dedupe: remembers keys it has processed before and drops repeats — the idempotency guard. Watch out: Cross-execution memory persists. After changing the key field, clear stored keys or old keys keep matching.

nodes.name: Keep Top Stories
nodes.notes: Caps the stream at 5 items to protect downstream quotas.

nodes.name: Rewrite for Our Audience (AI)
nodes.notes: Single fixed LLM step (no tool choice) — cheaper and more predictable than an agent.

nodes.name: OpenRouter Chat Model
nodes.notes: Chat model powering the AI step (model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5). Swap providers here without rewiring. Credential: OpenRouter API key. openrouter.ai/keys → create a key.

nodes.name: Publish to Telegram
nodes.notes: Sends a Telegram message to the configured chat — the same bot can also receive replies, so this doubles as a two-way ops channel. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Credential: Telegram bot token. Message @BotFather on Telegram → /newbot → copy the token.

nodes.name: Log Published Posts (Airtable)
nodes.notes: Creates a new record in Airtable's 'Emails' table. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Credential: Airtable PAT. airtable.com/create/tokens → create a Personal Access Token.

nodes.name: Align Field Names
nodes.notes: Normalizes field names so every source feeds the same downstream schema.

# Deliver a daily digest: Airtable

**Pattern:** Scheduled Digest · **Level:** Intermediate · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers newsletters work end to end across Airtable and Telegram.

It moves through 9 working steps, in this order:

1. Daily Schedule
2. Read Source Feed
3. Skip Already-Seen Posts
4. Keep Top Stories
5. Rewrite for Our Audience (AI)
6. OpenRouter Chat Model
7. Publish to Telegram
8. Log Published Posts (Airtable)
9. Align Field Names

## Why it exists

Doing newsletters work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Daily Schedule → Read Source Feed → Skip Already-Seen Posts → Keep Top Stories → Rewrite for Our Audience (AI) → OpenRouter Chat Model → Publish to Telegram → Log Published Posts (Airtable) → Align Field Names

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Airtable and Telegram aligned by hand for newsletters
- Newsletters work where "Read Source Feed" is still a manual step before Airtable
- Newsletters work that only reaches Airtable on a schedule, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Airtable and Telegram in step for newsletters, without anyone re-typing a row
- Safe to re-run: records already in Airtable or Telegram are skipped, across all 9 nodes of this newsletters build
- A failed Airtable or Telegram call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 9 nodes in this newsletters build
- The newsletters AI step is isolated from Airtable, so models swap without touching the other 9 nodes
- Pinned sample data ships with it — run all 9 nodes for newsletters before wiring Airtable

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Airtable PAT; OpenRouter API key; Telegram bot token.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Deduplication is cross-execution, not just within a single run — an RSS feed re-serves the same items on every poll, and without this the same story would get posted again on every scheduled check.

## Practice exercises

New to this pattern? Try these in order:

1. Turn off the AI rewrite step and compare the raw feed text against the rewritten version.
2. Add a second RSS source and merge both into one feed before dedupe.
3. Change 'Keep Top Stories' from 5 to 1 and see how it changes posting cadence.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**OpenRouter API key**
openrouter.ai/keys → create a key.
_Gotcha:_ One key reaches many models — handy for fallback.

**Telegram bot token**
Message @BotFather on Telegram → /newbot → copy the token.
_Gotcha:_ Get your chat ID by messaging the bot then opening api.telegram.org/bot<TOKEN>/getUpdates.

**Airtable PAT**
airtable.com/create/tokens → create a Personal Access Token.
_Gotcha:_ Scope the token to the specific base, and grant `data.records:write`. Field names are case-sensitive.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**AI node fails with an auth or quota error**
Cause: API key missing billing, or the per-minute rate limit was hit.
Fix: Confirm the provider account has credit. For rate limits, lower concurrency or switch to a higher-quota model.

**The AI returns the wrong shape or rambles**
Cause: The prompt is under-specified for the task.
Fix: Tighten the System Message: state the role, the constraints, and the exact output format you expect.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 When this fails

This starter workflow keeps things simple: no automatic retry or error branch yet. If a node fails, the execution just stops — open n8n's **Executions** tab to see which node and why. Ready to harden it? Turn on **Retry On Fail** (3 tries, 2s backoff) on the Settings tab of each external node, and add an error-output branch to a Slack/email alert — every Production-tier template in this library shows that exact pattern.

## 🤖 AI cluster

Purple nodes form one AI unit: the root node orchestrates, sub-nodes plug in via typed ports (model / memory / tools / parser). Swap the chat model without rewiring anything else. Costs scale with tokens — keep prompts lean and cap iterations.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your newsletters process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Airtable: scope the PAT to this one base and to `data.records:write`; a token scoped to the workspace can rewrite every base.
- Telegram: the bot token is a bearer credential — rotate it if it ever appears in an execution log.

**Do not log**
newsletters payloads carry personal data (names, email addresses, phone numbers). Log the record id and the outcome, not the record. n8n retains full execution data by default — turn that down for this workflow in Settings → Executions if these runs touch real contacts.
